**Not in this slice:**

## Why

Owners who use the pointer want to click tabs, rows and project keys. docs/dashboard.md:12 says mouse clicks do the same as keys. Decided: record 129 (ui.mouse): off in v1; if built, opt-in. Mouse capture also blocks terminal text selection, which matters for copying the slicer land command (docs/dashboard.md:102-103). Owner decision 2026-10-28 (interactive): the opt-in is a toggle key in the TUI, not a launch flag: `m` turns capture on and off at run time (off at every launch, not persisted), so selecting text is one key away. Bubble Tea v2.1: the mode is set on the View value (v.MouseMode), and clicks arrive as tea.MouseClickMsg.

## Failing tests

- TestMouseOffByDefault: View() leaves MouseMode off and a click message changes nothing (record 129).
- TestMouseKeyTogglesCapture: `m` sets MouseMode to cell motion, `m` again clears it; the status line says `mouse on` while it is on.
- TestMouseKeyIsInTheHintAndHelp; goldens for the help overlay.
- TestClickViewTabSwitchesView: a click on a view tab does what tab does.
- TestClickSidebarProjectSelectsIt: a click on a project row does what its digit key does.
- TestClickOverviewRowMovesCursor: a click on a row matches down-arrow movement to that row.
- TestClickOutsideRowsDoesNothing.
- TestClickWhileConfirmBarOrHelpOpenChangesNothing: ui.confirm (decided, #98) stays in charge.
- TestMouseKeyIgnoredInTextInput: `m` typed into an answer or filter field stays text.

## Implement

Tests first. Re-anchor from the code (view.go sets AltScreen; the key dispatch in model.go; the tab bar and sidebar renderers record their cell ranges). 1. Add `mouse bool` to Model (false at start), key `m` (free today) toggles it outside text input and the confirm bar; View() sets v.MouseMode = tea.MouseModeCellMotion when on. 2. Record hit rectangles while drawing: each view tab, each sidebar project row, each Overview/Running/Roadmap row (reuse the row-start bookkeeping from S151 and the selExtra scroll offset so a click lands on the drawn row, not the data row). 3. Handle tea.MouseClickMsg (left button) in Update: tab, sidebar row or list row, with the same effect as the key; ignore the wheel in this slice. Clicks do nothing while a confirm bar, help overlay or text field is open. 4. Status line shows `mouse on`; the hint bar offers `m mouse` low priority (dropLine high so it goes first); help overlay lists it (watch the 100x30 help headroom noted on S164). 5. docs/dashboard.md:12 and :102-103 name the toggle and the text-selection trade-off. UI slice: UI pass (r14).

Owner decision 2026-10-30 (interactive): the mouse toggle key is M, not m (S168 bound m to the Roadmap matrix pane; m matrix stays).
